Sara (ACME): Hey @Micah — since last night our embeddings QPS looks fine but vectors/sec dropped ~3x for a steady job. Tokens/sec is unchanged. Not seeing errors on our side.
Micah (support): sorry to hear that, can you paste a sample request + timing? Also which model/variant?
Sara (ACME): model: open-embed-1536, variant pinned to v2. Payloads identical, batch_size=64, concurrency=8. Quick curl we run:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["..."],"batch_size":64}'
```
Response time ~90ms per request but vectors/sec (measured by our consumer) drops from 12k -> ~4k.
Micah (support): interesting — tokens/sec same but vectors down suggests backend batching/kv-cache or GPU queueing. Can you share the request IDs for a couple of slow vs normal samples?
Sara (ACME): sent three request-ids in DM. Noticed service logs show intermittent AUTH 401s around the same window, then client retries. Could that cause backlog?
Anita (eng-runtime): retries alone usually don't drop vectors/sec unless they cause head-of-line blocking in the request router or reduce effective batch sizes. Jun — did any recent routing/autoscaler change roll out?
Jun (eng-sre): rolled a small change to per-tenant rate limiter yesterday (2026-03-16 23:40 UTC). It introduced a short-lived token refresh path that returns 202->401 on edge cases. Looking at metrics: when refresh fails, requests are retried synchronously which holds worker slots for ~1s each. Queue depth on GPU serving jumped.
DeployBot: deploy #deploy-2026-03-16-23:40 applied to rate-limiter-service.
Micah (support): can you share server-side snippet showing queue depth and batch window? Even a short paste will help.
Anita (eng-runtime): paste of kvcache/serving logs around spike:
```
2026-03-17T00:12:07Z [serve-gpu-12] kv_cache_acquire_wait_ms=1234 queue_depth=412 batches_flushed=98
2026-03-17T00:12:07Z [serve-gpu-12] auth_refresh_failures=7 auth_retries_sync=7
2026-03-17T00:12:08Z [serve-gpu-12] mean_batch_size=18 target_batch_size=64 effective_throughput_tokens=30000 tokens/s vectors/s=4200
```
Anita (eng-runtime): note mean_batch_size collapsed to 18 because many concurrent goroutines were blocked waiting for auth retries, so the serving runtime flushed smaller batches to meet latency SLOs -> vectors/sec dropped.
Sara (ACME): that matches our observation. Any workaround on our end?
Jun (eng-sre): short-term: increase client concurrency to rebuild batch fullness (not ideal), or retry logic with jitter so requests don't synchronize. Long-term: we should fix the sync retry path in rate-limiter.
Micah (support): created internal ticket INF-4912 to roll back the sync retry behavior and add idempotent async refresh. ETA ~2h for hotfix. I'll keep ACME posted.
Sara (ACME): thanks — appreciate the quick diagnosis. We'll hold off any client-side changes until you have the hotfix. :thumbsup:
Micah (support): action items:
- Jun/eng-sre rollback hotfix to async refresh (INF-4912)
- Anita/eng-runtime add metric to alert when mean_batch_size < 32 for >1m
- Jun add customer-visible incident note and communicate ETA to ACME
(Will update thread when hotfix is deployed)
